svg.text: Tarp Winch v4.2: Wiring Diagram (12 V DC, battery powered)
All power at the pool is extra-low-voltage DC from a battery. No mains wiring at the starting block. Charge away from the water.
IP67 BATTERY / CONTROLLER BOX (yellow box in the CAD, on the deck). Every cable leaves through an IP68 gland.
while the safety loop is made
Safety loop (purple): K1's coil only gets power
while every item in it is closed
pendant E-stop return feeds K1 coil +
IP67, wired straight to the battery
with its own 15 A fuse (charge only)
S4 E-STOP: N.C., in series with S2
IP67 roller lever on the base plate
N.C.: opens when the stopper ball
IP67 reed switch on the side plate,
magnet in the ball-lock pin handle:
closed only while the pin is in
Rounded tags with the same name
are the same wire. Dots = joined.
Lines that cross without a dot
1. Key S1, both E-stops (box S2, pendant S4) and fuse F2 form one series loop that powers K1's coil. Open any of them
and K1 drops out: the motor driver and the Pico lose power at the same moment.
2. Hold-to-run: the motor turns only while IN or OUT is held. The code ramps up over 0.5 s and stops when released.
3. Overload: above 30 A for 0.3 s it stops and beeps, so a snagged tarp can't rip the winch off the block.
4. S3 is normally closed, so a broken wire reads as 'limit reached' and winding IN is blocked (fails safe).
Crimp the stopper ball on the rope about 1 m before the tarp's tow bar.
5. S5 only closes while the ball-lock pin holds the spool's latch shut. Open or broken = the motor will not start.
6. Below 12.0 V the controller won't start. Recharge with a 14.6 V LiFePO4 charger, key OFF, away from the pool.
7. Mount F1 within 18 cm of battery +. D1 goes across the K1 coil; C1 sits right at the driver's power input.
8. The worm gearbox is self-locking: when power drops, the spool holds the tarp where it is.
Spool torque at 500 lbf, 3rd layer: 106 N·m
Trip 30 A ≈ 470 lbf on the last layer
≈ 9 Wh per pull → ≈ 13 pulls per charge
